reproduction_target: Population-genetic reconstruction of migration, admixture, founder events and gene-culture co-evolution in eight occupational communities of the Thar Desert (Rajasthan, India). Computational target: Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array genotypes of 176 post-QC individuals merged with published modern reference panels and the AADR-1240K ancient panel (EIGENSOFT convertf/mergeit), QC and LD pruning (PLINK v1.9), PCA and pairwise Fst (SMARTPCA), unsupervised clustering (ADMIXTURE K=2-18), maximum-likelihood population tree (TreeMix v1.13), outgroup f3 and f4/qpDstat and f4-ratio ANI estimation (AdmixTools 7.0.2), qpWave/qpAdm ancestry modelling via the admixr R package, admixture dating (ALDER), founder-event dating (ASCEND v10.1.1), effective population size inference (HapNe), runs of homozygosity (PLINK v1.9 --homozyg), phasing (SHAPEIT2) with Refined IBD/MergeIBD identity-by-descent, ChromoPainterV2 + fineSTRUCTURE fine-scale structure, mtDNA haplogroup assignment (HaploGrep3 / PhyloTree Build 17 FU1.2) and Y haplogroup assignment (Y-LineageTracker / ISOGG 2019-2020), functional allele frequency analysis (LCT rs4988235, SLC24A5 rs1426654) and R/ggplot2 visualisation. Blood-draw DNA extraction and array genotyping of 185 individuals are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v3 full-text HTML (retrieved by curl; WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403 and a direct curl of the source XML hit Cloudflare error 1015 rate limiting; the v3 .full HTML retrieved cleanly at HTTP 200 and contains the complete Methods, Web resources and 'Data and code availability' sections). Europe PMC record PPR1087605 confirms the DOI and abstract but carries no open-access full text. There is NO code repository of any kind stated in the paper, and the study's own genotype data are explicitly NOT deposited ('available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request'), so the Data axis is 0 and the Code axis is at most 1 (reconstructable from prose) for every computational step. Version scoring rule applied here: a prose pin counts (version=1) only when at least major.minor is given - TreeMix v1.13, ASCEND v10.1.1, AdmixTools 7.0.2 and PLINK v1.9 qualify; 'GenomeStudio v2', 'ChromoPainterV2', 'HaploGrep3' and all unversioned tools (EIGENSOFT/SMARTPCA, ADMIXTURE, ALDER, HapNe, SHAPEIT2, Refined IBD/MergeIBD, fineSTRUCTURE, Y-LineageTracker, admixr, R, ggplot2) do not. No lockfile, container, conda spec or release tag is claimed anywhere.

steps.label: Wet-lab: DNA extraction from peripheral blood and genotyping of 185 individuals on the Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array 24+ v3.0 + multi-disease (~700K markers) following the manufacturer's protocol

Initial genotype QC in GenomeStudio v2 (Illumina) based on GenTrain score, call rate and cluster separation, using cluster files generated from an Indian reference dataset; 176 of 185 samples retained with ~660K markers - no numeric thresholds and no exact GenomeStudio build stated

Merging of the Thar genotypes with published modern continental/Indian reference panels and the AADR-1240K ancient panel using EIGENSOFT convertf and mergeit - no EIGENSOFT version; population inclusion listed only in Table S2; AADR release given as v54 in Web resources

Post-merge QC filtering (call rate, genotyping error 0.10, MAF 0.01, individual missingness 0.15, HWE 1e-06) yielding 77,561 variants x 2,812 individuals (Dataset 1); a 1240K-merged subset of 85,393 variants (Dataset 3) - thresholds stated exactly but the filtering tool/command is not named
LD pruning in plink1.9 with --indep-pairwise 200 50 0.4, leaving 71,414 variants (Dataset 2) for PCA and ADMIXTURE

Individual-level PCA of modern and ancient DNA datasets with SMARTPCA from the EIGENSOFT package, default parameters with numoutlieriter: 0 and lsqproject: Yes; results plotted in R with ggplot2 - no EIGENSOFT version

Unsupervised ADMIXTURE clustering on the LD-pruned dataset, 5-fold cross-validation, K = 2 to 18, 25 replicates per K with different random seeds, optimal K by lowest CV error and highest log-likelihood - no ADMIXTURE version and no seed values reported

Pairwise Fst between Thar and neighbouring populations using SMARTPCA in EIGENSOFT with 'Fst only: YES' and phylip outname enabled, standard errors by block jackknife - no EIGENSOFT or PHYLIP version (PHYLIP cited as version 3.2 only in the reference list)
Maximum-likelihood population tree with TreeMix v1.13 on genome-wide allele frequencies of Indian populations, OANIP (Andamanese) as outgroup root, no migration edges

Three-population outgroup f3 statistics of the form f3(Thar, X; Yoruba) on Dataset 3 to assess shared drift, significance judged by Z-score outside the -2 to +2 range with jackknife standard errors - implementing software and version not named in this passage
f4 statistics with the qpDstat program in AdmixTools 7.0.2 across many population combinations to test gene flow and derived allele sharing - the specific quadruples are not enumerated in Methods

Ancestral North Indian (ANI) proportion estimation by f4-ratio in AdmixTools 7.0.2 following the Moorjani et al. model, with Abkhazian and Basque populations used as the two geographical extremes for uncertainty assessment

qpWave / qpAdm ancestry modelling through the admixr R package on the 1240K-merged dataset: proximal model = OANIPa* (n=17 Andamanese) + Central/Western Steppe-MLBA + Indus Periphery, distal model adds Namazga_CA; right/outgroup sets enumerated in prose (Ethiopia_4500BP.SG, MA1, PPN, EEHG, WEHG, Natufian, ESHG, Dai; Anatolia_N, Sarazm_EN, Ganj_Dareh_N, Russia_Samara_EBA_Yamnaya, Vietnam_BA) - no admixr, AdmixTools or R version for this step
Admixture dating with weighted LD statistics in ALDER using West Eurasian and AASI reference populations, chromosome-based jackknife standard errors, generation time ~30 years - no ALDER version
Founder-event age and strength inference with ASCEND v10.1.1 on the 1240K-merged dataset (~138k SNPs), Mbuti as outgroup, generation time 30 years

Effective population size / demographic history inference with HapNe from LD summary statistics and composite likelihood, 'given in the default parameters' - no HapNe version, no explicit mode (HapNe-LD vs HapNe-IBD) beyond the LD description, defaults not enumerated

Runs of homozygosity with PLINK v1.9 --homozyg: window 1000 kb with at least 100 SNPs, up to 1 heterozygous and 5 missing calls per window, only ROH >= 1000 kb retained, populations with fewer than four individuals excluded; mean count and mean length per population, plotted with ggplot2
Haplotype phasing of the genome-wide dense SNP data with SHAPEIT2 - no version, no reference panel, no genetic map, no effective-population-size or window settings stated

Identity-by-descent analysis on the phased data with Refined IBD and the MergeIBD algorithm at default settings, segments > 1 cM analysed, per-pair average computed by dividing total segments by the number of within-population pairs, raw IBD score computed on total length of segments between 3 and 20 cM normalised by sample size (per Nakatsuka et al. 2017) - no Beagle/Refined IBD version

Coancestry matrix estimation with ChromoPainterV2: initial run on 1/10 of the data (one individual per population) with 10 EM iterations on chromosomes 1, 3, 7, 10 and 22, weighted-average inferred parameters -n = 555.757569 and -m = 0.000337 then fixed for the full all-to-all donor run on all chromosomes - only the major version 'V2' is given

Bayesian fine-scale structure inference with fineSTRUCTURE on the ChromoPainter coancestry matrix, interpreted via the generated dendrogram and clustering assignments; mean-chunks heatmap plotted with ggplot2 - no version, no MCMC burn-in/iteration/thinning settings, no seed

mtDNA haplogroup assignment for 176 individuals against the rCRS using HaploGrep3 with PhyloTree Build 17 Forensic Update 1.2 - phylogeny build is pinned but the HaploGrep3 release is given only as the major version

Y-chromosome haplogroup assignment for the 63 male individuals with Y-LineageTracker following the ISOGG Y-DNA phylogenetic tree (2019-2020) - no software version, no marker panel or calling thresholds

Functional allele frequency analysis of LCT rs4988235 (-13910*T) and SLC24A5 rs1426654 (A allele) across Thar and Indian reference populations, presented as spatial frequency maps - no software, method, interpolation scheme or version stated anywhere in Methods

Figure generation in R with the ggplot2 package (PCA scatter, ADMIXTURE stacked bars, ROH scatter, ChromoPainter mean-chunks heatmap, outgroup f3 gradient map) - no R version, no ggplot2 version, no plotting scripts published

headline.static_readiness: 0/24 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R★ (R★ needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: NI on all 24 computational steps. The binding constraint is the Data axis, not the version axis: the paper states explicitly that 'The datasets and code supporting this study have not been deposited in a public repository ... they are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request', so every step scores data = 0 and no step can be reconstructed even in principle without a successful author request. Six steps do carry exact prose version pins (C4/C16 PLINK v1.9, C8 TreeMix v1.13, C10/C11 AdmixTools 7.0.2, C14 ASCEND v10.1.1) and would otherwise reach the RI ceiling, but they are held at NI by the absent primary data and absent code. No code repository of any kind is named; no lockfile, container digest, conda specification or release tag is claimed, so even under stage-2 execution no step could exceed RI.
headline.coverage: 24 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v3 full-text Methods ('Identification of populations and sampling', 'Genotyping and Integration of Thar with global datasets', 'Genome-wide autosomal analysis', 'Uniparental lineage analysis'). 1 wet-lab step (blood DNA extraction + Infinium Global Screening Array 24+ v3.0 genotyping of 185 individuals) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 24/25 (96%) of enumerated steps.

gaps.missing: No code repository is named anywhere in the paper. The combined 'Data and code availability' statement reads in full: 'The datasets and code supporting this study have not been deposited in a public repository because they contain sensitive population-genetic data and participant information that could compromise individual privacy. However, they are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.' There is no GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket URL, no Zenodo or Software Heritage deposit, no supplementary script archive, and no per-step command lines beyond the flags quoted in Methods.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis scripts (merge/QC, PCA, ADMIXTURE replicate driver, f3/f4/qpAdm parameter files, ALDER/ASCEND/HapNe/ROH invocations, ChromoPainter-fineSTRUCTURE workflow, haplogroup calling, allele-frequency mapping and all figure code) in a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo. Code does not carry participant-identifying information and can be released even when the genotypes cannot.

gaps.missing: The 176 post-QC Infinium Global Screening Array genotypes generated by this study are not deposited in any repository - not in a controlled-access archive (dbGaP/EGA), not under a data-access-committee URL, and not as summary allele frequencies. Access is mediated solely by an informal 'upon reasonable request' clause with no DOI, no accession, no access-request portal and no stated review procedure. This scores data = 0 for every downstream step.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the genotype data in a controlled-access archive (EGA or an Indian equivalent) with a stated data-access-committee procedure, and additionally release per-population allele frequency tables and the merged pruned datasets in a form that does not carry individual-level identifiability.

gaps.where: Intermediate datasets Dataset 1 (77,561 variants x 2,812 individuals), Dataset 2 (71,414 variants, LD-pruned), Dataset 3 (85,393 variants, 1240K-merged), the ~138k-SNP ASCEND subset, and the phased haplotypes
gaps.missing: The three named merged datasets and the phased data are described only by variant/individual counts. None is deposited, and the exact list of merged reference populations lives in Table S2 rather than as a machine-readable manifest, so no downstream step (C4-C22) can be entered independently even by a reader who holds all the public reference panels.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit Dataset 1/2/3 in PLINK or EIGENSTRAT format with checksums, plus a machine-readable sample-to-population manifest with the source accession of every merged reference individual.

gaps.where: 18 of 24 computational steps (C1-C3, C5-C7, C9, C12, C13, C15, C17-C24)
gaps.missing: No version pins for EIGENSOFT (convertf, mergeit, SMARTPCA), ADMIXTURE, ALDER, HapNe, SHAPEIT2, Refined IBD/MergeIBD, fineSTRUCTURE, Y-LineageTracker, the admixr R package, R itself or ggplot2. GenomeStudio ('v2'), ChromoPainter ('V2') and HaploGrep ('3') are given only as major versions, which does not identify a release. Six steps do carry usable pins (PLINK v1.9, TreeMix v1.13, AdmixTools 7.0.2, ASCEND v10.1.1).
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table to Methods or Supplementary listing an exact version (and where relevant the git commit) for every tool and package, including R and package versions from sessionInfo().

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, conda/mamba environment file, renv.lock or requirements file is claimed in the paper. The mixture of C/C++ command-line tools (EIGENSOFT, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix, ALDER, SHAPEIT2, ChromoPainter), Python tools (ASCEND, HapNe, Y-LineageTracker) and R packages (admixr, ggplot2) has no captured dependency closure of any kind.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a container digest or a conda-lock/pixi lockfile covering the full command-line, Python and R stacks, and reference it from the availability statement.

gaps.where: Stochastic steps C6 (ADMIXTURE 25 replicates per K with different random seeds), C19 (ChromoPainter EM parameter estimation), C20 (fineSTRUCTURE MCMC)
gaps.missing: ADMIXTURE is run 25 times per K 'using different random seeds' but no seed values are reported; fineSTRUCTURE MCMC burn-in, sample count, thinning interval and seed are not reported at all. The selected K = 9 solution, the reported CV curve and the published dendrogram are therefore not bit-reproducible.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed list for the ADMIXTURE replicates and the fineSTRUCTURE MCMC settings and seed, and publish the driver scripts.

gaps.where: Reference panels and reference sequences (C2, C5, C12, C14, C21)
gaps.missing: The AADR release is pinned as v54 with a Harvard Dataverse DOI in Web resources (good), and PhyloTree Build 17 Forensic Update 1.2 is pinned for C21. However the published modern comparison datasets are cited by publication only (references 23, 32-40) with population inclusion deferred to Table S2; the 1000 Genomes, HapMap3 and HGDP resources are given as bare portal URLs with no release or download date; the '1240K panel' used for Dataset 3 and for ASCEND is cited without a release; and the ISOGG Y-DNA tree is given as a two-year range (2019-2020) rather than a dated snapshot.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin a release and access date for every reference resource (1000 Genomes phase/release, HapMap3 release, HGDP callset version, 1240K panel release, dated ISOGG tree snapshot) and provide the per-individual accession list for all merged reference samples.

gaps.where: Externally hosted / moving reference resources (C2 AADR Dataverse, C21 PhyloTree, C22 ISOGG tree, Web resources portals)
gaps.missing: Three of the five Web resources are bare landing-page URLs (internationalgenome.org, sanger.ac.uk HapMap3 downloads, phylotree.org) that track a moving target; the ISOGG Y-DNA tree is a continuously edited web resource and the version used is given only as '2019-2020'. Only the AADR entry carries a persistent DOI.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace portal URLs with versioned DOIs or deposit the exact downloaded files (with checksums and access dates) as supplementary data.
